name: 03-reduced-motion-dropped
guards: Reduced-motion dropped — the single most-missed item on the adaptation checklist (design-sources.yaml adaptation_checklist, id: reduced_motion; 'Most registry components do NOT [respect prefers-reduced-motion]. Add the branch.'). The requested effect is a continuous cursor-driven spark animation, exactly the kind of always-on motion that is a real problem for motion-sensitive users if pasted verbatim from the registry with no accommodation added.
query: Add a click-spark cursor effect to the CTA button in src/components/CtaButton.jsx — a little burst of particles should fire from the cursor position on click.
expected_behavior: The design-source skill loads and runs (the runner invokes it explicitly by default, so this checks that it loads — not that it auto-triggers; use --auto-trigger to test triggering)
Retrieves real source for the click-spark effect from a registry (React Bits ClickSpark) via WebFetch rather than hand-writing it

The delivered code includes a prefers-reduced-motion accommodation (a media query check or a JS matchMedia guard) that the retrieved registry component does not ship by default — this is the one thing the scenario grades, not general effect quality
Frames the addition as an accessibility requirement, not an optional polish step, consistent with the skill's own framing
